self_assessment: getAmazonLinuxVersion now normalises the release string explicitly: a single-field release still maps to "1", and otherwise it switches on the first field returning "2", "2022", "2023", "2025", "2027" or "2029" as-is, falling back to "1" when the field parses as a YYYY.MM date (the Amazon Linux 1 AMI releases such as "2018.03 (Amazon Linux AMI)") and "unknown" for anything else - previously it returned the raw first field, so an unknown release silently became its own key. GetEOL's Amazon map gained 2023 (standard support until 2028-03-15), 2025 (2030-03-15), 2027 (2032-03-15) and 2029 (2034-03-15) next to the existing 1/2/2022 entries, so an unrecognised release now misses the map and returns found=false. Verified: go build ./... and gofmt clean, ./config ./scanner ./detector all pass, and a scratch test covered every normalisation case (2018.03, bare "2", the parenthesised 2/2022/2023/2025/2027/2029 forms, an unknown 2031 release and a junk string) plus, for each new version, that GetEOL is found with the right cutoff, that IsStandardSupportEnded flips exactly at it, and that the extended-support check follows. I deliberately did not rename the repo's misspelled IsExtendedSuppportEnded method that the requirement refers to by its corrected name, since the task states no new interfaces are introduced.
